To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bone metabolism markers are clinically useful for the management of bone metastasis in prostate cancer.
bone markers are useful surrogate biomarkers to detect bone metastasis and to predict prognosis in prostate cancer patients with bony metastasis.
bone turnover markers are useful for the assessment of bone metastatic spread, and are reliable surrogate markers to predict the prognosis for patients with prostate cancer with bone‐only metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the usefulness of bone metabolism markers in prostate cancer patients with skeletal metastasis.
the usefulness of bone turnover markers in prostate cancer patients with metastases to bone.
the usefulness of bone turnover markers in the management and treatment of prostate cancer with bone involvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bone markers are not only useful for monitoring bone metastatic spread, but also for predicting prognosis in patients with bone metastatic prostate cancer.
bone metabolism markers are useful for assessing bone metastases and for monitoring the efficacy of therapeutic agents for prostate cancer with bone involvement.
bone markers have a potential role in the management of prostate cancer with bone involvement, and are likely to be useful in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bone turnover markers are useful in the management of bone metastatic prostate cancer.
bone turnover markers are useful in clinical practice and clinical trials for prostate cancer with bone‐metastasis.
the use of bone metabolism markers in clinical practice is expected to improve the management of bone metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of bone markers in patients with prostate cancer with bone disease is a valuable tool to monitor bone metastases and to predict prognosis.
the use of bone markers may provide useful information in the clinical setting of bone metastatic prostate cancer.
bone turnover markers can be useful for monitoring the efficacy of new drugs for prostate cancer patients.
